provenance: All assets are generated in this repository. No third-party sample material is incorporated.

transforms.glass-crush: transposed two octaves down, driven and crushed
transforms.prism-impact: refracted into a C# minor chord

transforms.vox-chip: sliced from the open "ah" with a consonant-like attack

low.phase: bass-punch-cs settles in phase with sub-cs; trigger both on the same tick

sounds.name: GLASS HIT
sounds.role: Parent identity: bright tuned glass transient, sparkling 1.5–10 kHz halo over a pure C#5.
sounds.use: Exposed melodic hits, offbeat accents, call-and-response; velocity 0.45–0.9.
sounds.method: Eight split-pair glass modes (harmonic 1/2/4 core plus 2.756/5.404/8.933/13.34/18.64 bar modes) with ratio-dependent decay and a 1.2 ms band-limited strike.

sounds.name: GLASS REVERSE
sounds.role: Suction into a boundary: the same glass, bloomed through stereo diffusion, then reversed.
sounds.use: Ends exactly at the target; start 37,800 frames (two beats at 140 BPM) earlier; velocity 0.5–0.85.
sounds.method: Glass identity with 0.2 s body plus noise excited through its own mode resonators, per-channel allpass diffusion, reversed in float before PCM; 5 ms boundary taper.

sounds.name: GLASS CRUSH
sounds.role: The glass two octaves down, saturated and crushed into a dark tonal bass-call.
sounds.use: Rhythmic accents, bass-call answers on offbeats, layered under clap; velocity 0.5–0.9.
sounds.method: Glass identity at C#3 with a resample-length 0.3 s body and a 7-semitone falling onset; asymmetric tanh drive and 4.6-bit crush in parallel with the clean glass; closing resonant low-pass plus a falling 1.5 kHz to 650 Hz call resonance; all at 4x.

sounds.name: GHOST VOX
sounds.role: Synthetic airy "oh-ah" vowel; vocal character without a singer.
sounds.use: Phrase starts and answers, half-bar holds; chop with vox-chip; velocity 0.5–0.9.
sounds.method: Additive harmonics shaped by morphing five-formant envelopes, pitch scoop, delayed vibrato, +8 cent double and glottal-pulsed breath noise through the same formants.

sounds.name: VOX CHIP
sounds.role: An 85 ms slice of the ghost-vox "ah" with a consonant-like attack.
sounds.use: 1/16 stutters and chops at up to 160 BPM; velocity accents 0.4–0.9.
sounds.method: The ghost-vox voice function evaluated at its open "ah" (no vibrato), brightened first period, 0.6 ms attack, 20 ms decay and a 4 ms formant-filtered burst.

sounds.name: BASS PUNCH C#
sounds.role: Upper-bass attack: 277→69 Hz drop, C#2 harmonics through 1 kHz for small speakers, short body.
sounds.use: Layer with sub-cs at the same onset; kick role in half-time; velocity 0.6–1.
sounds.method: Exponential pitch drop with exactly two extra cycles (phase-locks to sub-cs), explicit decaying harmonics 2–8 through dynamic tanh drive, band-limited click.

sounds.name: SUB C#
sounds.role: Clean, stable 69.30 Hz sine body with controlled decay; no stereo or harmonics.
sounds.use: Same onset as bass-punch-cs; 37,800 frames = two beats at 140 BPM; space retriggers by a beat or more; velocity 0.6–1.
sounds.method: Zero-phase C#2 sine, 3 ms raised-cosine attack, 0.34 s exponential decay, 0.25 s cosine fade; identical phase to the settled bass-punch.

sounds.name: CHROME CLAP
sounds.role: Clap/snare hybrid: four uneven centered bursts, G#3 body, faint C#6 glass ring, mid/side tail.
sounds.use: Backbeat or half-time beat 3; ghost notes at 0.3–0.5; velocity 0.7–1.
sounds.method: Resonant band-passed noise bursts at 0/9.2/20.1/30.5 ms, 207.65 Hz pitched body, short glass identity at C#6 and a 75 ms tail with side-only decorrelation.

sounds.name: PIXEL HAT
sounds.role: Tight 6–12 kHz tick: high glass modes plus resonant noise; nothing below 2 kHz.
sounds.method: Glass identity modes at C#7 (2.756/4/5.404 ratios), two resonant noise bands at 8.4/11.5 kHz, 6.5 ms decay, four-pole 4.5 kHz high-pass.

sounds.name: PRISM IMPACT
sounds.role: Payoff: the glass refracted into a spread C# minor chord over a centered C#2 drop and soft air.
sounds.use: Final downbeat or section payoff; leave 1.8 s; velocity 0.7–1.
sounds.method: Six glass-identity tones (C#4 G#4 C#5 E5 G#5 C#6) with 3 ms dispersion, constant-power spread and allpass diffusion; mono 138→69 Hz boom, transient and closing air.
